result:
I would eliminate the human capacity to perceive other conscious beings as abstractions.

Most of the profound horrors in human history—war, systemic oppression, cruelty, exploitation, and the casual indifference that allows people to starve while resources rot—do not require sadism. They only require distance. Spatial distance, ideological distance, bureaucratic distance, or the simple evolutionary quirk that limits deep empathy to a small tribe while reducing everyone else to statistics, obstacles, or categories.

If that illusion vanished—if every person, particularly those who hold power, was cognitively and emotionally incapable of decoupling their decisions from the lived, somatic reality of the human beings on the receiving end—the machinery of cruelty would simply seize up. 

A politician could not order a strike, because the terror of the burning room would be too real to rationalize. An executive could not poison a watershed, because the sickness of the children drinking from it would be immediate, not a line item on an actuarial chart. 

It wouldn't eliminate natural disasters or biological disease, but it would instantly dismantle nearly all the suffering humanity deliberately manufactures for itself.
